Shodhana_Method.name: Bhavana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Bhavana is the process of triturating a powdered drug with liquid media such as herbal juice, decoction, cow urine, milk, or other prescribed liquids. Grinding continues until the liquid is completely absorbed and the material becomes soft and homogeneous. This process helps detoxify, enhance potency, and incorporate the therapeutic properties of the liquid medium into the drug.

Shodhana_Method.name: Swedana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Swedana involves heating the raw material in a liquid medium using mild heat, usually by boiling or steaming (often in a Dolayantra setup). The process removes impurities, reduces toxicity, softens the material, and facilitates further purification or processing.

Shodhana_Method.name: Nimajjana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Nimajjana is the immersion of a substance in a specific liquid medium for a fixed duration. This allows soluble impurities or toxic components to leach out into the liquid, making the material safer and easier to process.

Shodhana_Method.name: Mardana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Mardana is dry or semi-wet grinding of substances in a mortar and pestle, sometimes with minimal liquid. It reduces particle size, improves homogeneity, and may help reduce toxicity by physical transformation and intimate mixing.

Shodhana_Method.name: Bharjana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Bharjana is heating the drug in a pan, often without liquid or with minimal ghee or sand, until desired color or texture changes occur. This process removes moisture, reduces toxicity, and improves digestibility and stability.

Shodhana_Method.name: Dhalana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: In Dhalana, a substance is melted and then poured into a liquid medium such as oil, milk, or herbal decoction. The sudden cooling helps remove impurities and alter the physical structure, improving safety and medicinal properties.

Shodhana_Method.name: Nirvapa
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Nirvapa involves heating the material until red hot and then quenching it immediately in a liquid medium. This cycle may be repeated multiple times. It reduces hardness and toxicity, enhances brittleness, and facilitates further processing.

Shodhana_Method.name: Urdhva Patana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Urdhva Patana Shodhana is a purification method in which the volatile purified component is separated from impurities by upward sublimation and collected in an upper vessel through controlled heating.

Shodhana_Method.name: Bhavana with heating
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: This is a modified Bhavana where trituration with liquid media is combined with gentle heating. Heat accelerates chemical transformations, enhances absorption of the liquid medium, and improves detoxification and therapeutic efficacy.

Shodhana_Method.name: Nisechana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Nisechana is the process of rapidly cooling a heated material by immersing it in a liquid medium, which helps remove impurities and improves its physical properties for further processing.

Shodhana_Method.name: Nirmalikarana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: It is a specialized Shodhana process involving the dissolution, filtration, and recrystallization of a substance to remove physical impurities and obtain a purified crystalline product.

Shodhana_Method.name: Prakshalana
Shodhana_Method.Method_Description: Prakshalana is the process of thoroughly washing a drug with water or other prescribed liquids to remove surface impurities, dirt, soluble toxins, and unwanted residues.

Process.Process_Description: Marana is the calcination of purified metals and minerals through repeated cycles of grinding with herbal media and controlled heating (Puta). This converts the material into fine, ash-like Bhasma that is non-toxic, stable, and bioavailable.
Process.name: Marana

Process.Process_Description: Dhanyabhraka is a special purification method for mica in which powdered mica is mixed with rice grains, tied in cloth, and soaked or rubbed in water. The fine mica particles pass through the cloth while heavier impurities remain behind.
Process.name: Dhanyabhraka

Process.Process_Description: Amritikarana is a post-processing step applied to prepared Bhasma using ghee or herbal substances and mild heating. It is done to remove any residual toxicity, improve safety, and enhance therapeutic potency.
Process.name: Amritikarana

Process.Process_Description: Bhanupaka involves triturating the drug with liquid media and exposing it to sunlight. The mild heat and UV exposure promote slow drying and gentle chemical transformation.
Process.name: Bhanupaka

Process.Process_Description: Sthalipaka is cooking the drug with specific liquid media in a vessel over fire until the liquid evaporates. This helps detoxify the material and incorporate medicinal properties from the medium.
Process.name: Sthalipaka

Process.Process_Description: Dhavana is the repeated washing of a substance with water or other liquids to remove soluble impurities, dirt, and unwanted soluble components.
Process.name: Dhavana

Process.Process_Description: Jarana is roasting metals or minerals with herbal powders or other additives until they become brittle and powdery. It reduces hardness and prepares the substance for incineration (Marana).
Process.name: Jarana

Process.Process_Description: Prakshalana is the process of thoroughly washing a drug with water or other prescribed liquids to remove surface impurities, dirt, soluble toxins, and unwanted residues. It is usually performed as a preliminary or intermediate purification step before further processing.
Process.name: Prakshalana

Process.Process_Description: Bhavana is wet grinding of powdered drugs with herbal juices or decoctions until the liquid is fully absorbed. This enhances detoxification, potency, and homogeneity.
Process.name: Bhavana

Process.Process_Description: Lohitikarana is a treatment process that gives certain Bhasmas a reddish color through controlled heating and media treatment, indicating proper processing and improved therapeutic quality.
Process.name: Lohitikarana

Disease.Description: Acute prolapsed inter-vertebral disc (IVDP) is a painful condition that requires immediate treatment by conservative or surgical management. Though majority of patients show remission in symptoms with conservative treatment, regression of herniated disc with non-surgical management has been rarely reported.
Disease.name: Acute Prolapsed Inter-Vertebral Disc

Disease.Description: Acute upper limb ischemia (AULI) is a medical and surgical emergency involving sudden decrease in limb perfusion resulting in threat for limb viability. The approximate incidence of AULI is 1.5 cases/10,000 people per year.
Disease.name: Acute Upper Limb Ischemia

Disease.Description: Alopecia is the medical term for hair loss. It can mean small round patches missing from the scalp (alopecia areata), total loss of head hair (alopecia totalis), or loss of all body hair (alopecia universalis).
Disease.name: Alopecia

Disease.Description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) affects human life in various ways. ALS with multifocal onset might exhibit muscle stiffness and muscle weakness of upper and lower limbs, muscle twitching, atrophy, falling/tripping, slurred speech, difficulty in swallowing and loss of dexterity.
Disease.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

Disease.Description: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disorder that primarily involves the sacroiliac joints and the axial skeleton. There is also a variable involvement of peripheral joints and articular structures.
Disease.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis

Disease.Description: Anti-phospholipid antibody (APLA) syndrome is defined by the presence of thrombo-embolic complications and pregnancy morbidity in the presence of persistently increased titers of APLA syndrome.
Disease.name: Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome

Disease.Description: AIP is a rare disorder, its exact cause is unknown, but it is thought to be caused by the body's immune system attacking the pancreas and it responds to steroid therapy only.
Disease.name: Autoimmune Pancreatitis

Disease.Description: Avascular necrosis (AVN) of the bone is a condition characterized by the death or necrosis of bone tissue, accompanied by structural changes. It is also referred to as osteonecrosis or ischemic necrosis of the bone. It is mostly seen in patients having a history of excessive alcohol and high-dose steroid medications.
Disease.name: Avascular Necrosis

Disease.Description: Bell's palsy or Facial nerve palsy is a condition that causes temporary weakness or paralysis of the muscles in the face.
Disease.name: Bell's Palsy

Disease.Description: BPH is a nonmalignant enlargement of the prostate gland caused by excessive growth of the prostatic tissue and is the most common benign neoplasm of aging men mainly above 40 years.
Disease.name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia

Disease.Description: Bleeding piles (hemorrhoids) are swollen, inflamed blood vessels in the rectum or anus that often produce painless, bright red blood during bowel movements.
Disease.name: Bleeding Piles

Disease.Description: Bronchial asthma is a long-term lung disease that inflames and narrows the airways. It causes recurring bouts of wheezing, chest tightness, shortness of breath, and coughing.
Disease.name: Bronchial Asthma

Disease.Description: Central serous retinopathy (CSR), or central serous chorioretinopathy, occurs when fluid leaks under the retina, forming a small detachment that blurs or distorts central vision.
Disease.name: Central Serous Retinopathy

Disease.Description: Cerebral palsy is a group of permanent movement and posture disorders caused by abnormal development or damage to the developing brain, usually before or during birth.
Disease.name: Cerebral Palsy

Disease.Description: Cervical spondylosis is a degenerative condition of the cervical spine caused by age-related changes in the vertebrae, intervertebral discs, and surrounding structures. It may cause neck pain, stiffness, and restricted movement.
Disease.name: Cervical Spondylosis

Disease.Description: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy is a neurological condition caused by compression of the spinal cord due to degenerative changes in the cervical spine. It may result in weakness, sensory disturbances, impaired coordination, and difficulty walking.
Disease.name: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy

Disease.Description: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy is nerve damage resulting from certain anticancer drugs. It commonly presents with numbness, tingling, burning pain, weakness, or altered sensation, particularly in the hands and feet.
Disease.name: Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy

Disease.Description: Chronic alcoholism refers to prolonged and excessive alcohol consumption associated with dependence and adverse physical, psychological, and social consequences. It can affect multiple organs and may lead to neurological and metabolic complications.
Disease.name: Chronic Alchoholism

Disease.Description: Chronic low back pain is persistent or recurrent pain affecting the lower back for an extended period. It may be associated with spinal degeneration, muscular problems, nerve involvement, or other underlying conditions.
Disease.name: Chronic Low Back Pain

Disease.Description: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a type of blood cancer characterized by the abnormal accumulation of mature but functionally impaired lymphocytes, most commonly B lymphocytes. It generally progresses slowly and may initially produce few symptoms.
Disease.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia

Disease.Description: A chronic non-healing ulcer is a wound that fails to heal through the normal stages of tissue repair. It may persist because of factors such as poor blood supply, infection, diabetes, or repeated trauma.
Disease.name: Chronic Non-Healing Ulcer

Disease.Description: Chronic sinusitis is persistent inflammation of the paranasal sinuses lasting for an extended period. It commonly causes nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, facial pressure or pain, and reduced sense of smell.
Disease.name: Chronic Sinusitis

Disease.Description: Chronic urticaria is a condition characterized by recurrent episodes of itchy wheals (hives), with or without swelling, occurring without a consistently identifiable external trigger.
Disease.name: Chronic Urticaria

Disease.Description: Coma is a prolonged state of profound unconsciousness in which an individual cannot be awakened and does not respond normally to external stimuli. It may result from severe brain injury, stroke, metabolic disturbances, poisoning, or other serious conditions.
Disease.name: Coma

Disease.Description: COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). It primarily affects the respiratory system but can involve multiple organs and produce symptoms ranging from mild illness to severe disease.
Disease.name: Covid-19

Disease.Description: Depression is a mental health disorder characterized by persistent sadness or low mood, loss of interest or pleasure, and associated emotional, cognitive, behavioural, and physical symptoms that can interfere with daily functioning.
Disease.name: Depression

Disease.Description: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by elevated blood glucose levels resulting from inadequate insulin production, impaired insulin action, or a combination of both. Persistent hyperglycaemia can lead to complications affecting multiple organs.
Disease.name: Diabetes Mellitus

Disease.Description: A diabetic foot ulcer is a chronic open wound occurring on the foot in individuals with diabetes. It is commonly associated with diabetic neuropathy, impaired circulation, and delayed wound healing.
Disease.name: Diabetic Foot Ulcer

Disease.Description: Diabetic retinopathy is a complication of diabetes that affects the blood vessels of the retina. Progressive retinal damage can cause visual disturbances and, in advanced cases, significant vision loss.
Disease.name: Diabetic Retinopathy

Disease.Description: Diplopia, commonly known as double vision, is a visual disturbance in which a person perceives two images of a single object. It may occur due to abnormalities involving the eyes, ocular muscles, or the nerves controlling eye movement.
Disease.name: Diplopia

Disease.Description: Dyslipidemia is an abnormal level or composition of lipids in the blood, including elevated cholesterol or triglycerides and/or reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol. It is an important risk factor for cardiovascular disease.
Disease.name: Dyslipidemia

Disease.Description: Dysmenorrhea refers to painful menstruation, typically characterized by cramping pain in the lower abdomen during the menstrual period. It may also be accompanied by symptoms such as backache, nausea, or fatigue.
Disease.name: Dysmenorrhea

Disease.Description: Dysuria refers to painful, burning, or uncomfortable urination. It is commonly associated with infections or inflammation of the urinary tract but may occur due to other urinary or genital conditions.
Disease.name: Dysuria

Disease.Description: Eczema is a skin disorder characterized by Itching erythema, Scaling, Edema, vesiculation, and Discharge
Disease.name: Eczema

Disease.Description: Endometrial calcification refers to the abnormal deposition of calcium within the endometrial lining of the uterus.
Disease.name: Endometrial Calcification

Disease.Description: An endometrioma is a cyst formed when endometrial-like tissue grows within the ovary, commonly resulting from endometriosis.
Disease.name: Endometrioma

Disease.Description: Epidermolysis bullosa (EB) is a group of inherited rare skin disorders that causes the skin to become fragile and blister easily due to minor trauma or friction.
Disease.name: Epidermolysis Bullosa

Disease.Description: Episodic cluster headache is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent attacks of severe, usually one-sided headache, often accompanied by symptoms such as tearing, nasal congestion, or redness of the eye on the affected side.
Disease.name: Episodic Cluster Headache

Disease.Description: Psoriasis is a noninfectious chronic inflammatory skin disorder, characterized by well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery scales.
Disease.name: Erythrodermic Psoriasis

Disease.Description: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant tumor arising from the squamous epithelial cells lining the esophagus.
Disease.name: Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma

Disease.Description: Female infertility is the inability to achieve pregnancy after regular unprotected sexual intercourse for a defined period.
Disease.name: Female Infertility

Disease.Description: A fracture is a partial or complete break in the continuity of a bone, usually caused by trauma, excessive stress, or weakened bone. It may present with pain, swelling, deformity, and restricted movement.
Disease.name: Fracture

Disease.Description: Glaucoma is a group of eye disorders characterized by progressive damage to the optic nerve, often associated with elevated intraocular pressure.
Disease.name: Glaucoma

Disease.Description: Guillain Barre Syndrome (GB syndrome), a rare disease condition in which body’s immune system attacks part of the peripheral nervous system.
Disease.name: Guillain-Barre Syndrome

Disease.Description: Hemifacial spasm is a neurological disorder characterized by involuntary, intermittent contractions or twitching of the muscles on one side of the face.
Disease.name: Hemifacial Spasm

Disease.Description: Hepatitis B is a viral infection caused by the hepatitis B virus (HBV), primarily affecting the liver. It can cause acute or chronic liver inflammation and, in persistent cases, may lead to cirrhosis or liver cancer.
Disease.name: Hepatitis B

Disease.Description: Hirschsprung's disease is a congenital disorder in which certain portions of the large intestine lack normal nerve cells, resulting in impaired movement of intestinal contents.
Disease.name: Hirschsprung'S Disease

Disease.Description: Huntington's chorea is an inherited neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive movement abnormalities, particularly involuntary jerky movements called chorea, along with cognitive and psychiatric changes.
Disease.name: Huntington’S Chorea

Disease.Description: Hyperlipidemia refers to abnormally elevated levels of lipids in the blood, particularly cholesterol and triglycerides.
Disease.name: Hyperlipidemia

Disease.Description: Hypertension is a chronic condition in which blood pressure remains persistently elevated above the normal range.
Disease.name: Hypertension

Disease.Description: Juvenile spondyloarthritis is a group of inflammatory rheumatic disorders affecting children and adolescents, involving the joints and often the spine or areas where tendons attach to bone. It may cause pain, stiffness, swelling, and restricted movement.
Disease.name: Juvenile Spondyloarthritis

Disease.Description: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy is a group of inherited muscle disorders characterized by progressive weakness of the muscles around the hips and shoulders.
Disease.name: Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy

Disease.Description: Liver cirrhosis with ascites refers to advanced scarring of the liver accompanied by accumulation of fluid within the abdominal cavity.
Disease.name: Liver Cirrhosis With Ascites

Disease.Description: A low anti-Müllerian hormone level indicates reduced levels of AMH, a hormone produced by ovarian follicles and commonly used as a marker of ovarian reserve.
Disease.name: Low Anti-Mullerian Hormone (Amh) Level

Disease.Description: Lumbar disc herniation occurs when the inner material of an intervertebral disc protrudes through a weakened or damaged outer layer in the lower spine.
Disease.name: Lumbar Disc Herniation

Disease.Description: Lumbar myelomeningocele is a congenital neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the lumbar vertebrae.
Disease.name: Lumbar Myelomeningocele

Disease.Description: Lumbar spondylosis is a degenerative condition of the lumbar spine involving age-related changes in the vertebrae, discs, and facet joints. It may cause chronic low back pain, stiffness, and sometimes nerve-related symptoms.
Disease.name: Lumbar Spondylosis

Disease.Description: Major depressive disorder is a mental health condition characterized by persistent depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure, accompanied by emotional, cognitive, and physical symptoms that significantly affect daily functioning.
Disease.name: Major Depressive Disorder

Disease.Description: Meibomian gland dysfunction is a disorder in which the oil-producing meibomian glands of the eyelids do not function normally. It can destabilize the tear film and cause dry, irritated, burning, or gritty eyes.
Disease.name: Meibomian Gland Dysfunction

Disease.Description: Migraine is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent attacks of moderate to severe headache, often accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light or sound.
Disease.name: Migraine

Disease.Description: Myopia, or short-sightedness, is a refractive error in which distant objects appear blurred because light is focused in front of the retina rather than directly on it.
Disease.name: Myopia

Disease.Description: Nicolau syndrome is a rare injection-related complication characterized by severe pain and skin changes occurring shortly after administration of an injection.
Disease.name: Nicolau Syndrome

Disease.Description: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease is a condition characterized by excessive accumulation of fat in the liver in people without significant alcohol consumption.
Disease.name: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease

Disease.Description: Non-progress of labor refers to failure of labor to advance normally, such as inadequate cervical dilation or descent of the fetus despite ongoing labor.
Disease.name: Non-Progess Of Labor

Disease.Description: Obesity is a chronic condition characterized by excessive accumulation of body fat that may adversely affect health.
Disease.name: Obesity

Disease.Description: Oligoasthenozoospermia is a male reproductive condition characterized by reduced sperm concentration (oligozoospermia) together with reduced sperm motility (asthenozoospermia).
Disease.name: Oligoasthenozoospermia

Disease.Description: Oligomenorrhea refers to menstrual periods that occur at unusually long intervals, resulting in infrequent menstruation.
Disease.name: Oligomenorrhea

Disease.Description: Oligo-teratozoospermia is a condition affecting the normal sperm count and morphology leading to male factor infertility
Disease.name: Oligo-Teratozoospermia

Disease.Description: Oligozoospermia is a male reproductive condition characterized by a lower-than-normal concentration of sperm in the semen.
Disease.name: Oligozoospermia

Disease.Description: Oral submucous fibrosis is a chronic progressive disorder of the oral cavity characterized by inflammation and fibrosis of the mucosal tissues.
Disease.name: Oral Submucous Fibrosis

Disease.Description: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive deterioration of articular cartilage and changes in the underlying bone. It commonly causes joint pain, stiffness, swelling, and restricted movement.
Disease.name: Osteoarthritis

Disease.Description: Osteoporosis is a skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone strength and increased susceptibility to fractures. It commonly affects the spine, hip, and wrist.
Disease.name: Osteoporosis

Disease.Description: An ovarian cyst is a fluid-filled or solid sac that develops within or on the surface of an ovary.
Disease.name: Ovarian Cyst

Disease.Description: Papilledema is swelling of the optic disc caused by increased intracranial pressure.
Disease.name: Papilledema

Disease.Description: Polycystic ovarian disease is a condition characterized by multiple small follicles or cyst-like structures in the ovaries, often associated with hormonal and menstrual disturbances.
Disease.name: Poly Cystic Ovarian Disease

Disease.Description: Polycystic ovarian syndrome is a common endocrine disorder characterized by hormonal imbalance, irregular or absent ovulation, and clinical or biochemical features of excess androgen.
Disease.name: Poly Cystic Ovarian Syndrome

Disease.Description: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy is a disorder of the trigeminal nerve that develops following trauma or injury. It may cause persistent facial pain, numbness, tingling, or altered sensation in the affected area.
Disease.name: Post-Traumatic Trigeminal Neuropathy

Disease.Description: Post-traumatic trigeminal neuropathy is a disorder of the trigeminal nerve that develops following trauma or injury. It may cause persistent facial pain, numbness, tingling, or altered sensation in the affected area.
Disease.name: Prediabetes

Disease.Description: Primary insomnia refers to persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or obtaining restorative sleep that is not primarily explained by another medical or psychiatric condition.
Disease.name: Primary Insomnia

Disease.Description: Progressive bulbar palsy is a neurodegenerative disorder affecting the motor neurons controlling the muscles involved in speech, swallowing, and facial movements.
Disease.name: Progressive Bulbar Palsy

Disease.Description: Progressive supranuclear palsy is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by problems with balance, movement, eye movements, and postural control.
Disease.name: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy

Disease.Description: Prurigo nodularis is a chronic skin disorder characterized by intensely itchy, firm nodules that develop as a result of persistent scratching or rubbing. The lesions commonly occur on the arms, legs, and trunk.
Disease.name: Prurigo Nodularis

Disease.Description: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disorder characterized by well-demarcated, scaly plaques. It commonly affects the scalp, elbows, knees, and other areas and may also involve the joints.
Disease.name: Psoriasis

Disease.Description: Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disorder that primarily affects the joints. It commonly causes symmetrical joint pain, swelling, stiffness, and progressive joint damage.
Disease.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis

Disease.Description: Sciatica refers to pain along the distribution of the sciatic nerve, usually caused by irritation or compression of a nerve root in the lower spine. It commonly produces pain radiating from the lower back or buttock into the leg.
Disease.name: Sciatica

Disease.Description: Sclerosis refers to abnormal hardening or thickening of tissue due to pathological changes, such as fibrosis or scarring. The term can describe several different conditions depending on the affected tissue or organ.
Disease.name: Sclerosis

Disease.Description: Sinusitis is inflammation of the paranasal sinuses, often associated with nasal congestion, facial pressure or pain, nasal discharge, and reduced sense of smell.
Disease.name: Sinusitis

Disease.Description: Small fibre neuropathy is a disorder affecting small sensory and autonomic nerve fibres. It commonly causes burning pain, tingling, altered temperature or pain sensation, and sometimes autonomic symptoms.
Disease.name: Small Fibre Neuropathy

Disease.Description: Spinal cord injury is damage to the spinal cord resulting from trauma or other causes, potentially leading to impaired motor, sensory, and autonomic functions below the site of injury.
Disease.name: Spinal Cord Injury

Disease.Description: Spinocerebellar ataxia refers to a group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by progressive impairment of coordination and balance due to dysfunction of the cerebellum and related neural pathways.
Disease.name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia

Disease.Description: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 2 is an inherited neurodegenerative disorder caused by a genetic mutation affecting the nervous system.
Disease.name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2

Disease.Description: Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia tarda is a rare inherited skeletal disorder primarily affecting the spine and the growth and development of the ends of long bones.
Disease.name: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia Tarda

Disease.Description: Takayasu arteritis is a rare large-vessel inflammatory disease that primarily affects the aorta and its major branches.
Disease.name: Takayasu Arteritis

Disease.Description: Traumatic optic neuropathy is damage to the optic nerve resulting from trauma to the head or eye. It can cause sudden or progressive reduction in vision and other visual disturbances.
Disease.name: Traumatic Optic Neuropathy

Disease.Description: Trigeminal neuralgia is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent, sudden episodes of severe, brief, electric-shock-like pain affecting one or more branches of the trigeminal nerve, usually on one side of the face.
Disease.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia

Disease.Description: Tubal blockage refers to obstruction of one or both fallopian tubes, preventing normal movement of the egg and sperm through the reproductive tract. It is an important cause of female infertility.
Disease.name: Tubal Blockage

Disease.Description: Type 2 diabetes is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by elevated blood glucose levels due primarily to insulin resistance and progressive impairment of insulin secretion.
Disease.name: Type 2 Diabetes

Disease.Description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is the same metabolic condition commonly referred to as type 2 diabetes, characterized by persistent hyperglycaemia resulting from insulin resistance and inadequate insulin secretion.
Disease.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

Disease.Description: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by inflammation and ulceration of the lining of the colon and rectum. It commonly causes abdominal pain, diarrhoea, rectal bleeding, and urgency.
Disease.name: Ulcerative Colitis

Disease.Description: Ulcerative keratitis is an inflammatory condition of the cornea associated with corneal ulceration. It may cause eye pain, redness, photophobia, tearing, and impaired vision and requires prompt medical attention.
Disease.name: Ulcerative Keratitis

Disease.Description: Urethral stricture is abnormal narrowing of the urethra caused by scar tissue or other structural changes. It can obstruct urinary flow and cause difficulty or discomfort during urination.
Disease.name: Urethral Stricture

Disease.Description: Urinary incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine due to impaired control of bladder storage or emptying.
Disease.name: Urinary Incontinence

Disease.Description: Uterine fibroid is not only the commonest benign tumour of uterus but also the commonest solid tumour in female that usually found in approximately 20 to 40% women of reproductive age group,1 start as multiple, single cell seedlings distributed throughout the uterine wall.
Disease.name: Uterine Fibroids

Disease.Description: Vasculitis is chronic inflammation resulting in necrosis of blood vessels due to narrowing or occlusion of the lumen.
Disease.name: Vasculitis

Disease.Description: A venous ulcer is a chronic wound that commonly develops on the lower leg due to impaired venous circulation and increased pressure within the veins. It is often associated with swelling, skin changes, and poor wound healing.
Disease.name: Venous Ulcer

Disease.Description: A wound is a disruption or injury to the normal structure and integrity of body tissue, usually involving the skin or underlying tissues. It may result from trauma, surgery, infection, or other pathological processes.
Disease.name: Wounds

Disease.Description: Pityriasis rubra pilaris is a rare chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by reddish-orange scaly patches, follicular papules, and areas of relatively normal skin. It may involve the scalp, face, trunk, and limbs.
Disease.name: Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris

Disease.Description: An acute renal calculus refers to the sudden clinical presentation of a kidney stone, formed by crystallization of substances within the urinary tract.
Disease.name: Acute Renal Calculus

Disease.Description: Rett syndrome is a rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorder that primarily affects females. It is characterized by normal early development followed by loss of acquired skills, impaired communication, repetitive hand movements, and problems with coordination.
Disease.name: Rett Syndrome

Disease.Description: Neurogenic bladder is a dysfunction of bladder storage or emptying caused by abnormalities of the nervous system. It may result in urinary retention, urgency, frequency, or involuntary urine leakage.
Disease.name: Neurogenic Bladder

Disease.Description: Knee osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disorder involving progressive deterioration of the cartilage and other structures of the knee. It commonly causes knee pain, stiffness, swelling, and difficulty with movement or walking
Disease.name: Knee Osteoarthritis

Disease.Description: Irritable bowel syndrome is a functional gastrointestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain associated with changes in bowel habits, including diarrhoea, constipation, or both, without an identifiable structural cause.
Disease.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome

Disease.Description: A lumbo-sacral disorder refers to a condition affecting the lumbar and sacral regions of the lower spine. It may cause lower back pain, stiffness, restricted movement, or nerve-related symptoms affecting the lower limbs.
Disease.name: Lumbo-Sacral Disorder

Disease.Description: Piles, also known as haemorrhoids, are swollen and enlarged veins in the lower rectum or anus. They may cause rectal bleeding, discomfort, itching, or a lump around the anal region.
Disease.name: Piles

Disease.Description: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is the gradual irreversible damage to kidney function that occurs in both kidneys. This disease is marked by a sustained kidney damage or decreased functioning for at least three months.
Disease.name: Chronic Kidney Disease

Disease.Description: Lumbar spinal stenosis is abnormal narrowing of spinal canal at lumbar region, may occur as a result of progression of spondylotic changes.
Disease.name: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis

Disease.Description: Diabetic neuropathy symptoms include pain, numbness, reduced sensation of touch or oversensitivity, uncomfortable tingling and burning, skin ulcer and reduced reflexes.
Disease.name: Diabetic Neuropathy

Disease.Description: A child with global developmental delay is unable to attain developmental milestones owing to brain damage which leads to impairment in gross and fine motor, personal social, speech, and activities of daily living.
Disease.name: Global Developmental Delay

Disease.Description: Haemorrhoids are swollen and enlarged veins in the lower rectum or anus. They may cause rectal bleeding, pain or discomfort, itching, and swelling around the anal region.
Disease.name: Haemorrhoids

Disease.Description: Post-thrombotic syndrome is a chronic complication of deep vein thrombosis caused by damage to the veins and their valves.
Disease.name: Post-Thrombotic Syndrome

Disease.Description: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a or musculoskeletal condition characterized by chronic widespread musculoskeletal pain and tenderness including associated neuropsychological symptoms including fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, cognitive dysfunction, anxiety, and depression.
Disease.name: Fibromyalgia

Disease.Description: Bipolar Affective Disorder (BPAD) is a recurrent and chronic disorder that is characterized by episodes of depression and elevated mood with intervening periods of normal mood.
Disease.name: Bipolar Affective Disorder

Disease.Description: Adhesive capsulitis often referred to as frozen shoulder, is one of the long term complication of Diabetes mellitus which causes gradual loss of motion in shoulder.
Disease.name: Adhesive Capsulitis Stage 2

Disease.Description: Necrozoospermia (also called necrospermia) is a rare semen disorder where most or all of the sperm present in a semen sample are dead or non-viable.
Disease.name: Necrozoospermia

Disease.Description: Vipadika or Vaipadika is explained as one among Eleven Kshudra Kushtas (Minor skin ailments) which has the features of Paanipaada sputana (Cracking of palms and soles) associated with Teevravedana (Intense pain) as explained by Acharya Charaka.
Disease.name: Vipadika

Disease.Description: Hemiplegia is the commonest manifestation of a Stroke with neurological deficit affecting the face, limbs and trunk on one side or either side of the body.
Disease.name: Hemiplegia

Disease.Description: Lumbar disc disease (LDD) is a common cause of chronic or recurrent low back and leg pain, most frequently affecting the L4–L5 and L5–S1 levels. The pain may be localized to the lower back or may radiate to the leg, buttocks, or hip.
Disease.name: Lumbar Disc Disease

Disease.Description: Hirayama disease (HD) is a juvenile nonprogressive amyotrophy disease. It is characterized by gradual onset of muscular dystrophy in the distal part of the upper limbs related to flexion movements of the cervical spine.
Disease.name: Hirayama Disease

Disease.Description: Infertility is the inability to achieve pregnancy after regular unprotected sexual intercourse for a specified period. It may result from factors affecting ovulation, reproductive organs, sperm function, hormonal balance, or other reproductive factors.
Disease.name: Infertility

Disease.Description: Senile dementia is a syndrome due to disease of the brain, usually of a chronic or progressive nature, in which there is disturbance of multiple higher cortical functions, without any impairment in consciousness. Prevalence rates for senile dementia increase essentially with advancing age.
Disease.name: Senile Dementia

Disease.Description: Psoriasis vulgaris, commonly known as plaque psoriasis, is the most frequent form of an autoimmune skin condition. It causes the rapid buildup of skin cells, leading to raised, inflamed patches covered with silvery-white or gray scales.
Disease.name: Psoriasis Vulgaris

Disease.Description: Visphota Kushta is a traditional Ayurvedic classification for blistering skin diseases characterized by thin-skinned, transparent, or fluid-filled vesicles and bullae.
Disease.name: Visphota Kushta

Disease.Description: Scalp psoriasis is a common, chronic autoimmune condition where an overactive immune system speeds up skin cell growth.
Disease.name: Scalp Psoriasis

Disease.Description: Psychogenic pseudo-myasthenic ptosis is a rare functional neurological (conversion) symptom where a person experiences a drooping eyelid that mimics myasthenia gravis, but has psychological rather than physical origins.
Disease.name: Psychogenic Pseudomyasthenic Ptosis

Formulation.Description: Haridra [Curcuma longa L], Sunti [Zingiber officinale ROSC.], Maricha [Piper nigrum LINN.], Pippali [Piper longum LINN]. Twak [Cinnamomumzeylanica BLUME.] and other drugs made into granule forms with jaggery
Formulation.name: Haridrakhantam

Formulation.name: Icchabhedi Ras

Formulation.name: Kachuradi Churna

Formulation.name: Kalyana Kshara

Ingredients: Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Vibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), Amalaki (Emblica officinalis), Vishala (Citrulus cholocynthis), Bhadra ela (Amomum subulatum), Devadaru (Cedrus deodara), Elavaluka (Prunusavium), Sariva (Hemidesmus indicus), Haridra (Turmeric), Daruharidra (Berberis aristata), Shalaparni (Desmodium gangeticum), Prishnaparni (Uraria picta), Phalini (Callicarpa macrophylla), Nata (Valeriana wallichi), Brihati (Solanum indicum), Kushta (Saussurea lappa), Manjishta (Rubia cordifolia), Nagakeshara (Mesuaferrea), Dadimaphalatwak (Punicagranatum), Vella (Embeliaribes), Talisapatra (Abbies webbiana), Ela (Elettaria cardamomum), Malati (Jasminum sambac), Utpala (Nympheastellata), Danti (Baliospermum montanum), Padmaka (Prunus poddum), Hima (Sandalwood - Santalum album), Sarpi (Ghee - 768 g)

Formulation.name: Kapikacchu Beeja Churna

Formulation.Description: seasoned vegetable soup

Formulation.name: Krutavedhana Yoga
Kwatha Of Amalaki, Yashtimadhu, Shatavari, And Madhu

Dosha.Description: Vata is the Dosha responsible for movement and regulation of bodily activities, including breathing, circulation, nerve functions, movement of limbs, and elimination. It is predominantly composed of Air and Space elements.
Dosha.name: Vata

Dosha.Description: Pitta is the Dosha responsible for digestion, metabolism, transformation, and maintenance of body temperature. It is predominantly composed of Fire and Water elements.
Dosha.name: Pitta

Dosha.Description: Kapha is the Dosha responsible for stability, strength, lubrication, nourishment, and structural integrity of the body. It is predominantly composed of Water and Earth elements.
Dosha.name: Kapha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic description of inability or difficulty in obtaining normal sleep, commonly associated with aggravated Vata and disturbed mental factors.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Anidra

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder in which Apana Vata obstructs the normal functioning of Vyana Vata, leading to disturbed movement and circulation-related functions.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Apanavrita Vyanavata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata-dominant headache disorder characterized by severe pain affecting one half of the head, often occurring episodically.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Ardhavabhedaka

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: In Ayurveda, Ardita is a disease with functional disturbances affecting the Uthamanga (head) and stands close with the symptoms of Bell's palsy. It is narrated as one among the Asheeti Vata Vikaras (80 types of typical vata predominant diseases).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Ardita

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder characterized by reduced quantity or deficient formation of Artava (menstrual tissue), often presenting with scanty or delayed menstruation.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Artava Kshaya

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A state of depletion of Asthi (bone tissue) and Majja (marrow/nerve-related tissue) associated with weakness and degenerative manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Asthi-Majja Kshaya

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder in which aggravated Vata is located in the bone and marrow tissues, producing pain, weakness, and degenerative symptoms.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Asthimajjagata-Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Pathological disturbance of the channels responsible for nourishment and functioning of bone tissue (Asthi).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Asthivaha Srotodushti

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Vata disorders produced by obstruction of the normal movement of Vata by another Dosha, tissue, or bodily factor.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Avarana Janya Vata Vyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder resulting from trauma to the urinary/bladder region considered a vital anatomical site (Basti Marma).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Bastimarm Abhighataja Vatavyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic description of a mass or nodular swelling involving the testicular region (Beejakosha).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Beejakosha Granthi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic term for fracture or disruption of the continuity of a bone, generally associated with trauma.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Bhagna

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Infertility described as resulting from depletion or inadequate nourishment of the bodily tissues (Dhatus) affecting reproductive capacity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Dhatukshayajanya Vandhyata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A chronic or complicated form of nasal disorder with persistent discharge and inflammation, described under Pratishyaya.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Dushta Pratishyaya

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A chronic or contaminated/non-healing wound characterized by abnormal discharge, inflammation, pain, or delayed healing.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Dushta Vrana

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ekakushtha is a type of Kshudrakushtha representing minor skin disorders that are typically less severe but still require attention.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Ekakushtha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Vata disorders arising from depletion of bodily tissues, allowing Vata to become aggravated and produce pain, weakness, and functional disturbances.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Dhatukshayajanya Vatavyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A reproductive disorder characterized by recurrent loss or expulsion of pregnancy, resulting in inability to sustain pregnancy.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Garbhasravi Vandhyatva

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder of Grahani, the functional site of digestion and intestinal retention, characterized by impaired digestion and irregular bowel movements.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Grahani Dosha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata-dominant condition characterized by stiffness, restricted movement, and pain in the neck region.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Greevastambha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic Vata disorder characterized by pain radiating from the lower back through the buttock and along the leg, often associated with stiffness and restricted movement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Gridhrasi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Indralupta is a disease characterized by patches of hair loss spread throughout the body and scalp.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Indralupta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A condition described by accumulation of fluid within the abdominal cavity, producing abdominal distension and associated systemic manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Jalodara

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Swelling caused predominantly by aggravated Kapha, characterized by heaviness, pallor, coldness, and relatively stable edema.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kaphaja Shotha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Kapha-dominant form of Unmada (mental disorder) characterized by lethargy, excessive sleep, heaviness, and diminished mental activity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kaphaja Unmada

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A blistering skin disorder involving all three Doshas with predominance of Kapha and Pitta, producing eruptions or blisters.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kapha-Pitta Dominant Tridoshaja Visphota

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A condition in which Kapha obstructs the normal function of Udana Vata, affecting speech, effort, strength, and upward bodily functions.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kaphavruta Udanavata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder caused by obstruction of Vata by aggravated Kapha, resulting in impaired Vata movement and associated heaviness and sluggishness.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kaphavruta Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A menstrual disorder characterized by painful menstruation, commonly associated with aggravated Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kashtartava

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder characterized by stiffness, restricted movement, and pain in the lower back region.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kati Graha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A degenerative Vata disorder affecting the lumbosacral joints, producing pain, stiffness, and restricted movement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kati Sandhigata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Kitibha Kushta, which is characterized by reddish patches, indurated, Itching, and Scaling.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kitibha Kushta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An acute skin manifestation characterized by raised, itchy eruptions or wheals, associated with Dosha disturbance and resembling urticarial lesions.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kotha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ksheena Shukra is one of the “Shukradushti” (~vitiation of sperm) where Shukra Dhatu (~reproductive tissue) is of poor quality.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Ksheena Shukra

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Prameha disorder characterized by frequent urination with urine having characteristics resembling honey, traditionally associated with deranged metabolism and predominantly Vata involvement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Madhumeha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A chronic, difficult-to-heal wound associated with Madhumeha, characterized by delayed healing and abnormal tissue changes.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Madhumehajanaya Dushta Vrana

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A visual disorder described as disturbance or impairment of vision associated with Madhumeha, reflecting ocular complications of the condition.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Madhumehajanya Timira

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A group of severe or major forms of Kushtha (chronic skin disorders) described in classical Ayurvedic texts.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Maha Kushta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Mandala Kushtha a type of Maha Kushtha is a chronic of Kushtha
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mandala Kushtha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder in which aggravated Vata is located in Mamsa (muscle tissue), producing pain, stiffness, twitching, or weakness.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mansagata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder involving abnormal accumulation or disturbance of Meda (adipose/fat tissue), associated with metabolic imbalance and excessive body weight.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Medoroga

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic urinary disorder characterized by painful or difficult urination, often associated with inflammation or obstruction of the urinary tract.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mootrakruchchhra

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: In Ayurveda, Mutraghata has been defined as a syndrome of obstructive urinary pathology due to deranged function of Vata Dosha, particularly Apana Vata (a type of Vata responsible for excretory function).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mutraghata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A condition characterized by retention or obstruction of urine, with incomplete or delayed urinary evacuation.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mutrasanga

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder in which aggravated Vata is localized in the large intestine (Pakvashaya), producing abdominal pain, constipation, distension, and altered bowel function.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Pakvashayagata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A group of Ayurvedic metabolic and urinary disorders characterized by excessive or abnormal urination and derangement of bodily tissues, with Madhumeha representing an important subtype.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Prameha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder caused by obstruction of Vyana Vata by Prana Vata, disturbing normal circulation and coordinated bodily movements.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Prana Avrutta Vyana

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A classical wasting disorder characterized by progressive tissue depletion, weakness, cough, fever, and respiratory or systemic manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Rajayakshma

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A condition characterized by passage of blood with loose stools, reflecting involvement of Rakta and intestinal pathology.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Raktatisara

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder in which Rakta (blood tissue) obstructs the normal movement of Vata, producing pain and vascular or inflammatory manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Raktavrita Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A degenerative Vata disorder affecting the joints, characterized by pain, stiffness, restricted movement, and sometimes joint crepitus.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sandhigata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Disorders arising from excessive nourishment, overnutrition, and accumulation of Doshas and bodily tissues, commonly associated with obesity and metabolic disease.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Santarpanajanya Vyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A severe state of loss of consciousness or profound collapse of mental and physical functions, described as a serious Vata-related condition.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sanyasa

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder in which aggravated Vata affects the entire body, producing generalized pain, stiffness, weakness, or functional impairment.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sarvanga Gatavata Vyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A generalized Vata disorder characterized by widespread involvement of the body with pain, stiffness, weakness, and impaired movement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sarvangavata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A generalized disorder of the oral cavity, involving widespread inflammation or lesions of the oral tissues.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sarvasara Mukharoga

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic ocular disorder characterized by whitish discoloration or opacity affecting ocular structures, resulting in visual disturbance.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Savrinashukla

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A skin disorder characterized by itchy, raised eruptions associated with exposure to cold, traditionally involving Vata and Kapha with Pitta involvement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sheethapitta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder arising from trauma to vital structures of the head (Shiro Marma), potentially producing neurological or sensory disturbances.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Shiromarmabhighata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A form of Arsha (haemorrhoidal disorder) associated with bleeding, characterized particularly by rectal bleeding.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Shonitarsha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic term for inflammatory swelling or edema, characterized by enlargement, discomfort, and Dosha-specific features.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Shotha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder affecting the blood vessels or vascular channels (Sira), producing pain, obstruction, or abnormal vascular manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Siragata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic disorder characterized by excessive accumulation of Meda and increased body bulk, accompanied by impaired metabolism and reduced physical capacity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sthaulya

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A metabolic form of Prameha characterized by excess body tissue and obesity-associated manifestations, commonly involving Kapha and Meda.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Sthula Prameha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A headache disorder characterized by pain that increases with the rising intensity of the sun and decreases as the sun sets, traditionally associated with Vata-Pitta.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Suryavarta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Tamaka Shwasa is a type of Shwasa Roga (respiratory disease) affecting the Pranavaha Srotas and characterized by Pratiloma Vayu (prolonged expiration), Ghurghuraka (wheeze), Ativa Tivra Vagam Ca Shwasam Pranaprapidakam (dyspnoea of exceedingly deep velocity, which was immensely injurious to life).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Tamaka Shwasa

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic neurological condition described by involuntary or abnormal movements of the body, associated predominantly with aggravated Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Tandava Roga

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic ocular disorder characterized by progressive disturbance or diminution of vision, described according to the stage and Dosha involvement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Timira

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A form of Jaundice (Kamala) described as affecting both pathways or systems involved in the movement of bile, producing generalized yellow discoloration and related symptoms.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Ubhayapatha Ashrita Swatantra Kamala

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A gynecological disorder caused by upward or abnormal movement of Apana Vata, leading to menstrual pain, obstruction, or disturbed reproductive functions.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Udavarta Yonivyapada

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic description of a tumor-like mass (Arbuda) occurring on the left side of the body, particularly the left flank or thoracic region depending on the clinical context.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vamaparshwa Arbuda

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic term for female infertility, describing inability to achieve or sustain conception due to disturbance of reproductive factors.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vandhyatva

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An ocular condition characterized by contraction or abnormal narrowing of the eyelid, potentially interfering with normal eyelid movement and eye protection.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vartma Sankocha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder of Rakta (blood tissue) caused predominantly by Vata and Pitta vitiation, producing inflammatory, vascular, or skin-related manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vata Pitta Pradhana Rakta Pradoshaja Vikara

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A broad group of disorders caused predominantly by aggravated or disturbed Vata, commonly presenting with pain, stiffness, weakness, tremors, or impaired movement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vata Vyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Swelling predominantly caused by Vata aggravation, typically associated with pain, variable swelling, dryness, and irregularity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vataja Shopha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder caused by interaction of aggravated Vata and Rakta, classically presenting with severe joint pain, redness, swelling, and burning sensations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vatarakta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: a skin problem mentioned in Ayurvedic literature with Kapha and Pitta morbidly/pathology
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vicharchika

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A wasting or depletion disorder characterized by loss of strength and bodily tissues, generally associated with prolonged illness or Dosha imbalance.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vikshay

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A severe or deep form of Vatarakta, in which Vata and Rakta involvement extends into deeper tissues and produces intense pain and inflammation.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Gambhira Vatarakta

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A type of Kushtha characterized by large, pale or reddish-white lesions resembling the petals of a lotus (Pundarika).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Pundarik Kushtha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A type of Kushtha characterized by large, pale or reddish-white lesions resembling the petals of a lotus (Pundarika).
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mutrasmari

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A urinary disorder described as abnormal constriction or obstruction involving the urinary bladder and urinary passage, leading to disturbed urine flow.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Basti Kundalika

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder affecting the knee joint, characterized by pain, stiffness, restricted movement, and degenerative changes.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Janu Sandhigata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder characterized by stiffness and restricted movement of the neck, commonly involving the cervical region.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Manyasthambha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A condition characterized by pain in the lower back or lumbar region, predominantly attributed to aggravated Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Katishool

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic term for haemorrhoids, characterized by abnormal growths or swellings in the anal region, which may be painful or bleeding.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Arsha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder localized in the bones and structures of the cervical region, producing neck pain, stiffness, and restricted movement.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Greeva Asthigatavata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A broad group of urinary disorders involving abnormalities in urine formation, flow, quantity, or elimination.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mootra Dosha Vikar

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder characterized by stiffness and restricted movement in the Trika region, corresponding broadly to the lumbosacral/pelvic area.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Trikagraha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Khalitya in Ayurveda is a disease in which Pitta, combining with Vata and entering the pores of the hairs (hair follicles), causes hair fall, and then Kapha, along with Rakta, obstructs the pores of those hairs, making it impossible for other hair to grow.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Khalitya

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder associated with impaired development or reduced strength in childhood, involving inadequate growth and functional capacity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Bala Samvardhana Janya Vata Vikruti

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder attributed to depletion of Mastulunga, traditionally associated with brain/cranial tissue, producing neurological manifestations.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mastulunga Kshaya Janya Vatavyadhi

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disorder in which aggravated Vata is localized in muscle tissue, causing pain, stiffness, twitching, or weakness.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mamsagata Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata-dominant form of Unmada (mental disorder) characterized by restlessness, abnormal speech or behaviour, fear, and disturbed mental activity.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Vatika Unmada

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A disease that usually affects the amsa sandhi (shoulder joint) is produced by vitiated vata dosha.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Avabahuka

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Pakshagata is an important Vatavyadhi described under Vataja nanatmaja vyadhi and Mahavatavyadhi  can manifest either due to dhatukshaya and margavarana
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Pakshagata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Kaphavrutavyana Vata is an Ayurvedic pathological condition that occurs when Kapha dosha obstructs the normal functioning of Vyana Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Kaphavrutavyana Vata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Pathological disturbance of the Artavavaha Srotas, the channels responsible for formation and transport of reproductive/menstrual tissue, causing menstrual and fertility-related disorders.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Artavavaha Srotodushti

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic description of a tumor-like mass arising in the uterus (Garbhashaya), representing an abnormal uterine growth.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Garbhashaya Arbuda

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: An Ayurvedic term used to describe childhood developmental delays and growth disorders
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Bala Samvardhana Vikara

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: In Ayurveda, Mutramarga Sankocha can be understood as constriction or narrowing of the urinary passage due to derangement of Doshas, predominantly Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Mutramarga Sankocha

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: Ayurvedic description of loss or severe impairment of vision caused by Vata aggravation following trauma to the eye or visual apparatus.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Abhighatajanya Vataprakopaj Drishtinash

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A digestive disorder described as impaired digestion with stagnation of improperly digested food, associated mainly with aggravated Kapha and Vata.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Alasaka

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A systemic disorder caused by Ama associated with aggravated Vata, characterized mainly by joint pain, stiffness, and swelling.
Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.name: Amavata

Ayurvedic_Diagnosis.Description: A Vata disorder described by pain and stiffness affecting the neck and shoulders, with possible radiation toward the head and upper limbs.

Shodhana_Type.Description: Samanya Shodhana (General purification) is the preliminary, common purification step applied to many metals, minerals, and toxic herbs using standard media such as water, cow urine, milk, oil, or herbal decoctions. Its purpose is to remove visible impurities, reduce basic toxicity, and make the material softer and suitable for further processing.
Shodhana_Type.name: Samanya Shodhana

Shodhana_Type.Description: Vishesh Shodhana (Specific purification) is the drug-specific purification performed after Samanya Shodhana. It uses special media and procedures tailored to a particular substance to eliminate its unique toxic components and enhance its therapeutic safety and efficacy.
Shodhana_Type.name: Vishesha Shodhana

USES_MEDIA.Procedure: The processed seeds were triturated with fresh lemon juice in a mortar–pestle for 1 hour daily for 3 days and air-dried after each cycle to obtain a uniform paste.
Crude Hingula was triturated with lemon juice seven times until dark red color developed, then washed and dried.
Raw Rasaka was triturated with lemon juice until completely dried, the process repeated 7 times, then washed with water to remove acidity and dried.
Tuttha was purified by triturating with lemon juice for 6 hours, then dried and collected as shodhita Tuttha.
The powdered Shodhita Jayapala was levigated with fresh lemon juice three times, shade-dried, and stored for further use.

The powdered cotyledons were soaked/levigated with fresh lemon juice for 3 days with daily replenishment of the juice, then the paste was dried on the outer surface of a mud pot in sunlight to reduce excess oil content.
The purified Tuttha was ground with sufficient lemon juice for 6 hours and then dried to obtain Shodhita Tuttha.
Dried Rakta-Snuhi latex was triturated with tamarind leaf juice in ratios of 8:4, 8:2, and 8:1 and repeatedly dried in sunlight or shade for three cycles.

Raw Shilajit was triturated (levigated) sequentially with Yavakshara solution until uniform, dried, then again triturated with Kanji and dried, and finally levigated with cow urine followed by drying to obtain purified Shilajit.

Raw Shilajit was triturated (levigated) sequentially with Yavakshara solution until uniform, dried, then again triturated with Kanji and dried, and finally levigated with cow urine followed by drying to obtain purified Shilajit.
Kasisa powder was triturated with fresh Bhringaraja (Eclipta Alba) Juice until dry, and the process was repeated three times using fresh juice each cycle.
Nirmalikrita Tuttha was continuously triturated with Citrus Medica Juice for 6 hours, adding fresh juice as needed, and then dried to obtain purified Tuttha.
Tuttha was thoroughly ground with fresh citrus medica juice until completely processed and dried to obtain Shodhita Tuttha.

Raw Shilajit was triturated (levigated) sequentially with Yavakshara solution until uniform, dried, then again triturated with Kanji and dried, and finally levigated with cow urine followed by drying to obtain purified Shilajit.
Manahshila was triturated with ginger juice repeatedly seven times (total ~660 mL for 250 g) until thoroughly processed.
The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth (pottali) and subjected to boiling in cow’s milk at 60 °C for 3 hours, followed by washing and air-drying.
The seeds tied in a muslin cloth were subjected to boiling in cow’s milk for 6 hours, then washed with hot water, shade-dried, and powdered.
The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and were boiled in cow's milk for 6 hours, followed by cleaning, husk removal, and subsequent extraction.
The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and were exposed to milk vapors over boiling cow's milk for 3 hours, followed by lukewarm washing and shade drying.
The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and were boiled in cow's milk for 3 hours, followed by washing and shade drying.
5 g of powdered root tied in muslin cloth was suspended in boiling cow milk for 5 hours.
200 g of coarse powder tied in cloth was boiled in cow's milk for 5 hours.
100 g seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and boiled in fresh cow’s milk (≈7 L) at 100°C for 6 hours, followed by washing, decortication, and shade drying.
100 g seeds tied in a muslin cloth were completely immersed in cow’s milk (6 L) and boiled at 100°C for 3 hours, followed by washing, removal of seed coat and embryo, drying, and pulverization.
The roots are boiled in cow’s milk for 12 hours, then the cortical layer is removed and the drug is washed with water.
The aconite roots were boiled in milk, followed by washing with water and drying.
Dehulled and powdered Croton tiglium seeds were tied in a cloth bundle and boiled in milk for 3 h, then washed and dried; the process was repeated three times for purification.
Seeds tied in cloth were boiled in milk for 3 h, washed, peeled, embryo removed and cotyledons powdered.
Next Dhaturra seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and were subjected to boiling in cow's milk for 3 hours.
The seeds were tied in a muslin cloth and boiled in cow's milk for 3 hours, followed by washing, drying, decortication, and pulverization.
The seeds tied in a muslin cloth were subjected to boiling in cow’s urine for 12 hours, followed by washing and drying to obtain purified seeds.
Small root pieces were tied in a Pottali and subjected to boiling in cow milk for 3 1/2 hours, with continuous heating and replenishing of milk, followed by washing, drying, and powdering.

Total protein content (Abrin) reduced by ~36.5-44.7%, maximum in Kanji-Shodhita samples, indicating significant removal of toxic protein.
Total protein content decreased by 96.59–99.78% after Shodhana, with the greatest reduction in Kanji-treated samples, indicating marked reduction of the toxic protein (abrin)

Both groups receiving 500 mg/day Shilajit for 21 days showed a significant reduction in blood glucose levels in newly diagnosed hyperglycemic subjects, indicating effective hypoglycemic activity for both purification methods.

Shodhita Bhanga significantly reduced pain (84.1%), anxiety, and depression, improved quality of life, and showed no major adverse effects, dependency, or withdrawal symptoms. In contrast, unprocessed Cannabis is associated with habit formation and cognitive impairment, indicating that Shodhana improves its safety and therapeutic efficacy.
Processed samples (especially milk-treated) significantly prolonged sleeping time without convulsions, showing reduced toxicity and enhanced CNS depressant activity.
Processed samples reduced locomotor activity in a controlled manner at sub-convulsive doses, indicating safer CNS depressant action.
Crude drug hastened convulsions (4.75 min), whereas processed samples significantly delayed onset (up to 11.25 min in milk-treated), demonstrating anticonvulsant transformation.
Diazepam completely prevented lethality of processed samples at LD₁₀₀ doses, confirming manageable and reduced neurotoxicity after Shodhana.
Processed samples antagonized morphine-induced catalepsy while crude potentiated it, indicating beneficial neuropharmacological modification.
Overall alkaloid content reduced in processed samples (A > B > C > D), supporting chemical detoxification.
Shodhana produced an ~70% reduction in total alkaloid content in both Datura metel and Datura innoxia, confirming effective detoxification.

Shankha Bhasma purified with lemon juice showed significantly higher symptom resolution (66 to 71% vs. 27 to 31%, P < 0.005) and more heartburn-free days, confirming improved therapeutic efficacy after proper Shodhana.
Absence of red colour in spent purification media (appearing only after acid digestion) confirms ferric ions were removed as chelated complexes, proving detoxification.
Toxic metals (As, Cd, Hg, Pb) remained within permissible limits in Badrashma Pishti, confirming safety for therapeutic use.
Anacardol increased from 47.51% to 50.62% after Shodhana, suggesting decarboxylation of toxic anacardic acid into the less toxic anacardol, thereby supporting detoxification.
Reduced from 35.40% to 28.71% w/w, suggesting removal of irritant oil constituents during Shodhana.

THC ( Delta 9-tetrahydrocannabinol) content decreased by 26–85% after Shodhana, depending on the purification method, confirming significant removal of the narcotic principle. The greatest reduction (85%) was achieved by washing the leaves until free from turbidity followed by frying in ghee, indicating this as the most effective detoxification method.
Toxic albumins and globulins were present before Shodhana but absent after Shodhana, confirming detoxification.

Protein content of the seeds decreased from 8.73% to 6.51%, while the protein content of the Shodhana milk increased from 4.76% to 7.99%, indicating the transfer of proteinaceous toxic constituents (including abrin) from the seeds into the processing medium during Shodhana.

Microscopic analysis showed that Shodhana reduced glandular trichomes (the major site of tetrahydrocannabinol, THC, accumulation), along with fragmented fibers, reduced cystoliths, and shrunken/distorted epidermal cells, indicating structural modifications associated with reduced psychoactive THC content and detoxification.
No treatment-related toxicity or adverse clinical effects were observed at therapeutic or higher doses, confirming good long-term safety.
Overall toxicity assessment showed that Tuttha Bhasma was well tolerated at the therapeutic dose, with no dose-dependent toxicity, confirming the safety of the properly prepared Bhasma.

Purified Bhallataka exhibited greater thrombolytic activity (66.59% clot lysis) than raw Bhallataka (59.82%), demonstrating that Shodhana enhances the thrombolytic efficacy while producing a safer form of the drug.
XRPD confirmed transformation of raw coral and demonstrated reduced crystallite/particle size after repeated grinding and calcination, indicating structural modification during Marana.

XRPD showed complete transformation of calcium carbonate from the aragonite phase in raw Mukta Shukti to the more stable calcite phase in Mukta Shukti Bhasma, with minor portlandite [Ca(OH)₂] formation.

ICP-MS analysis showed that Shodhana markedly reduced silver (5138 to 119.5 ppm), copper (2866.1 to 0.5324 ppm), and tin (0.371 to 0.3233 ppm) impurities, producing purified mercury with elemental composition closer to commercially available mercury.
Chemical analysis showed an increase in sulfur content from 89.39% to 97.14% after Shodhana, confirming improved purity of Sulphur.
Amino acid content was reduced after Shodhana, with no detectable amino acids in the distilled water-treated Guñjā samples, confirming depletion of proteinaceous constituents.
Strychnine and brucine were detected in the post-Shodhana milk, confirming removal of the principal toxic alkaloids from Nux-vomica seeds during Shodhana.
